title: Salvage dead Main node and set up SSH to LAN nodes
displayTitle: Salvage dead Main node and set up SSH to LAN nodes
goal: set Load Legacy Option ROM to Disabled - ok - did that can ReX run this card? (should be back now)
outcome: Checked the disk on the adapter again — it's byte-for-byte unchanged from before: #1 EFI System 0.20 GB #3 NTFS "D:" 297.16 GB (Windows 11) #2 MSR 0.02 GB #4 Recovery 0.72 GB So whatever that installer erased, **it wasn't this disk.** Mint went somewhere else — one of three places: 1. **The machine's internal disk.** Most likely. If that box has its own drive, "erase disk" took that one. 2. **The Ventoy stick itself.** This happens more than people admit — booting from the stick, the installer offers the stick as a target and it gets picked. Everything "works," and the machine it runs on has nothing. 3. **Nowhere** — if it never reached the end, a half-written ESP plus no root. Here's the ten-second way to know. diary.text: The user set Load Legacy Option ROM to Disabled and asked whether the RX card could run, then widened the session into fleet hardware work: a full hardware report for Jim on the XPS node, onboarding a second white Dell XPS ("XPSW", Windows 10, roughly a GTX-1060, at 192.168.1.142), making that GTX-1060 usable, and finding a home for a spare RX6800 freed when Main died. Across about 13 hours and 285 messages (25 user turns, 120 tool calls) the work ran through SSH with the id_ed25519_echidna key against 192.168.1.142, an scp of hwinv.ps1, PowerShell Win32_DiskDrive and CIM queries, fleetctl.py scan, newnode.py, and lpr_print.py status checks against the printer at 192.168.1.253. C:\AI\fleet\ accumulated roster.json, newnode.py, diskwipe.ps1, diskdebug.ps1, diagnose.ps1 and diagnose2.ps1, fanprobe.ps1, gpucheck.ps1, fixvcredist.ps1, finalize.ps1, a bench/mine set (bench1060, bench2, bench7b, benchcpu, benchcuda, mine1060, mine2, minediag), and the write-ups jim-xps-report.txt and jim-xpsw-report.txt. The last thread is unresolved: a Linux Mint install on the white XPS looked like it erased a disk, but re-checking the adapter showed it byte-for-byte unchanged — #1 EFI System 0.20 GB, #3 NTFS "D:" 297.16 GB (Windows 11), #2 MSR 0.02 GB, #4 Recovery 0.72 GB — so the installer wrote somewhere else, and the session closed with three candidates rather than an answer: the box's internal disk, the Ventoy stick, or nowhere at all. The next action is to boot that machine and run lsblk -o NAME,SIZE,MODEL,FSTYPE,LABEL,MOUNTPOINT to see where Mint actually landed.
